skill.name: salesforce-development
skill.description: Guidance for Salesforce development patterns, including Lightning Web Components, Apex triggers, Queueable Apex, APIs, Connected Apps, and Salesforce DX packaging.
skill.summary: Build Salesforce features with Apex, LWC, async processing, and deployment patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only skill file. Manual review found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or instructions to bypass security review.

content.user_title: Build Salesforce Apps with Apex and LWC
content.value_statement: Salesforce teams need consistent patterns for Apex, LWC, async jobs, and packaging. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for platform development tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains Lightning Web Component patterns using the wire service and reactive data binding.
Guides bulkified Apex trigger design with handler classes and recursion prevention.
Describes Queueable Apex use for asynchronous processing, monitoring, and job chaining.
Supports Salesforce API, Connected App, scratch org, and 2GP packaging discussions.
Highlights common Salesforce anti-patterns such as SOQL, DML, and hardcoded IDs.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts, CLI commands, or automated Salesforce org access.
Does not validate code against a live org, metadata API, or current package state.
Provides concise pattern guidance, not full Salesforce documentation or release notes.
Requires project-specific context for sharing rules, limits, integrations, and naming standards.

use_cases.title: Design LWC Data Access
use_cases.description: Plan a Lightning Web Component that uses reactive data binding and appropriate Apex or Lightning Data Service sources.

use_cases.title: Review Apex Trigger Architecture
use_cases.description: Check whether trigger logic is bulkified, separated into handlers, and prepared for recursion control.

use_cases.title: Plan Package Delivery
use_cases.description: Discuss scratch org workflows, Salesforce DX structure, and 2GP packaging choices before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Salesforce Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain when to use the LWC wire service instead of imperative Apex. Include key tradeoffs and a short review checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Apex Trigger Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Apex trigger approach for bulkification, handler separation, recursion prevention, and testability. Suggest practical improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Async Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Queueable Apex approach for this business process. Cover payload shape, chaining limits, AsyncApexJob monitoring, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Salesforce Delivery Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this Salesforce DX and 2GP delivery plan. Identify packaging risks, scratch org workflow gaps, API concerns, and release readiness checks.

output_examples.input: Review our Opportunity trigger design for bulk safety.
output_examples.output: The response identifies SOQL and DML placement risks, recommends a handler pattern, and lists tests for 200-record transactions.

output_examples.input: Plan an LWC that displays account data and refreshes when records change.
output_examples.output: The response compares Lightning Data Service and Apex wire methods, then gives a concise component design and review checklist.

output_examples.input: Decide whether Queueable Apex fits a nightly integration handoff.
output_examples.output: The response explains Queueable Apex fit, notes chaining limits, and recommends monitoring and retry considerations.

best_practices: Provide object names, trigger context, expected data volume, and existing automation before asking for Apex guidance.
Ask for governor limit, testability, and rollback considerations when reviewing Salesforce designs.
Verify recommendations against your org policies, Salesforce release version, and package governance.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for trigger code without sharing data volume, recursion risks, and related automation.
Do not treat pattern guidance as proof that code passes Salesforce security review.
Do not hardcode Salesforce IDs, org-specific URLs, or unmanaged assumptions into generated designs.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to Salesforce?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-only skill and does not access Salesforce orgs, APIs, files, or credentials.

faq.question: Can it write complete Apex or LWC code?
faq.answer: It can guide code generation through the AI tool, but users must review, test, and adapt all output.

faq.question: Which Salesforce topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers LWC wire patterns, Apex trigger design, Queueable Apex, APIs, Connected Apps, Salesforce DX, and 2GP packages.

faq.question: Is this suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. Beginners can ask for explanations, while experienced teams can use it for design review prompts.

faq.question: Does it replace Salesforce documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use official Salesforce documentation for release-specific limits, syntax changes, and certification requirements.

faq.question: Is it safe for customer data?
faq.answer: The skill contains no data access logic. Users should avoid pasting secrets, personal data, or confidential customer records.
